title: The baby steps
principle: Work through money goals in a strict order, one at a time, instead of splitting attention across all of them at once: a small starter emergency fund first, then aggressive debt payoff, then a full emergency fund, and only after that, investing and other goals. The sequencing is the point — it removes the paralysis of trying to save, pay off debt, and invest simultaneously.
formula: Below a starter fund target, nearly all free cash goes to savings; with debt outstanding, extra cash prioritizes payoff; once a full emergency fund is reached, free cash shifts toward investing.
fitsWhen: You feel overwhelmed by competing money goals and want a strict, motivating order to follow rather than juggling several percentages.
critique: The strict sequencing can be mathematically suboptimal — paying off low-interest debt before investing, for instance, can cost more in forgone returns than it saves in interest — but the approach trades some optimality for behavioral momentum and simplicity.
